correctness.rationale: The two Artin–Schreier equations define a smooth genus-five curve with unique rational infinity: pole order seven, degree-two extension, genus from different exponent eight; projective gradients are independent. The exact count formula 1+2 times a trace-zero set is valid in each finite field. Five counts suffice by Newton identities and genus-five functional equation. Standalone exhaustive standard-library checker tests all 192 quadruples, 14 coefficient classes and multiplicities, field irreducibility, slope calculations and independent direct counts over F4,F16,F64 for selected parameters. The finite universe is exhaustively checked; no infinite-field extrapolation is asserted.

value.rationale: The locus is a newly studied four-dimensional genus-five family with a live geometric Newton-stratification motivation. F4 is the smallest nontrivial extension of F2, yielding a natural complete finite arithmetic classification not covered by the published F2 census. The theorem gives all 14 complete Weil polynomials with exact presentation multiplicities (therefore all point counts over all extensions for each F4 form), 14 rational Jacobian isogeny classes, and a precise Newton boundary. This constitutes a meaningful exact finite classification with reproducible use as a benchmark; no global theorem beyond F4 is claimed.
